IaaS, PaaS, SaaS.

#separator:: IaaS vs SaaS — who has more responsibility?
column2: IaaS = most customer responsibility; SaaS = least. You always own data + identity.

#separator:: What does the customer own in EVERY service model?
column2: Their data and identities (and access configuration).

#separator:: IaaS: who patches the guest OS?
column2: The customer (provider only covers hardware, hypervisor, facility).

#separator:: PaaS: what does the provider manage that IaaS doesn't?
column2: The OS and runtime; customer keeps app/config + data + identity.

column2: 2379 — key-value store holding Secrets; unauthenticated read = full cluster compromise.

#separator:: kubelet port and risk if exposed?
column2: 10250 — node agent; exposed = exec into pods on that node.

#separator:: Why is a container weaker isolation than a VM?
column2: It shares the host kernel (namespaces/cgroups/caps/seccomp), so escape is realistic.
